title: Close the frontend source-of-truth sweep with committed scope and behavioral rate/billing proof

acceptanceCriteria.description: All 42 reverified findings are committed with severity, rule, unsafe owner, canonical owner, imperfect-data entry point, disposition, caller, and executable proof.
Rate selection, eligibility, selected-rate proof, and client rate-source identity remain backend-owned; cross-order, cross-account, and stale-fact attempts fail before provider activity.
Invoice header totals and cancelled/return treatment remain owned by the backend billing read model and are proven for cardinality, idempotency, and repeat runs on PostgreSQL-compatible fixtures.
The three missing owners called out during the sweep—client rate-source policy, billing invoice totals, and reporting-window presets—are canonical backend services consumed by thin routes or UI.
PS-433 is mandatory in the source-of-truth guard pack, and the full pack, strict typecheck, and production web build pass at the reviewed implementation SHA.
Verification is offline and non-mutating: no live provider request, label purchase, postage charge, marketplace notification, production database write, or shipped/cancelled data mutation occurred.

oldOwners.delegatesTo: backend-issued rate DTO, selected-rate proof, and eligibility facts

oldOwners.path: web/src/components/Views/AnalysisView.tsx and BillingView.tsx local reporting-window presets

wrappers.delegatesTo: backend API DTOs and commands without ranking, minting proof, or recomputing authoritative totals
backend row workflow, rate proof, and display facts

sotBypass.details: The frontend remains a display/action consumer. Rate, label, billing, client rate-source, reporting-window, and shipped/cancelled safety truth remains in named backend owners; no wrapper selects or persists alternate truth.

evidence.proves: The committed replacement for the missing transient artifact contains exactly 42 unique findings, split 15 High and 27 Medium, with every required placement and proof field populated.
Real backend snapshot, fingerprint, purchase-account, and client rate-source owners integrate with an injected provider boundary; valid backend proof reaches it exactly once.
Cross-order selected-rate keys, cross-account purchase identity, mismatched request facts, and cross-client rate-source identity are rejected before the provider spy is touched.
The real invoice-totals owner runs against a current-column PostgreSQL-compatible fixture and returns stable totals without changing line cardinality.
Cancelled non-return charges, retained return charges, out-of-window rows, another client's rows, duplicate order lines, and repeat reads cannot corrupt invoice cardinality or totals.
The static ownership sweep and both behavioral boundary suites execute as one focused PS-433 command.
Best-rate ranking, proof issuance, and client consumption remain bound to the canonical backend rate authority.
Billing formula callers continue to delegate authoritative invoice totals to the backend owner.
The complete mandatory source-of-truth pack passes with PS-433 wired into both the runner and its guard-of-guard.
Backend and frontend strict TypeScript checks pass.
The production frontend bundle builds successfully with 2,989 modules transformed.

The reviewed evidence commit contains only PS-433 documentation, offline tests, and guard/package wiring. It touches no product runtime, provider adapter, migration, or protected shipped/cancelled surface.

verification.command: No migrations were added or modified; not applicable.

migrations.rollbackPlan: Revert the packet-only commit, then revert 55a3440f8baa68f339ef81f20c4510e5aee10b1b; no schema or production-data rollback is required.

rollback.strategy: Revert the packet-only commit and PS-433 evidence commit. This removes only the committed scope matrix, offline proofs, documentation, and guard wiring; the already-deployed product implementation remains unchanged.

liveVerification.reason: This closure pass adds offline review evidence only. It intentionally does not invoke live rate providers, purchase labels or postage, notify marketplaces, or mutate production billing or shipped/cancelled records; deployment health is verified separately after push.
